hits.snippet: In 2021, Airtable was valued at $11.7 billion. This week, it agreed to be acquired by Bending Spoons at a $1.285 billion enterprise value. The story in three moments: 2021 -> valued at $11.7B at the very top of the SaaS boom, on a fresh $735M round. Early 2026 -> shares changing hands on the secondary market around $4B. This week -> a definitive agreement to sell to Bending Spoons at a $1.29B enterprise value, roughly $2.25B to shareholders once you add the cash on the balance sheet. All cash, not yet closed. The obvious read is: Airtable lost almost 90% of its peak valuation. The more useful question is: Who actually lost what and who had already taken money off the table?
